what_it_is: A Stanford method paper on cutting the cost of querying commercial LLM APIs (p. 1). It outlines three strategies, prompt adaptation, LLM approximation and LLM cascade (pp. 2-5), and instantiates the cascade as FrugalGPT: a query goes to a list of LLM APIs in order, and a learned generation scoring function returns the first answer whose reliability score exceeds that API's threshold, otherwise the next API is queried; the list and the thresholds are optimised under a budget (pp. 5-6). With a DistilBERT regressor as the scorer and cascades of length 3 over 12 APIs, it matches the best single LLM at 59.2% to 98.3% lower cost on three datasets, or raises accuracy over GPT-4 at the same cost (p. 1, Table 3 p. 8).
domain: LLM inference cost; tasks: financial-news classification (HEADLINES), legal overruling classification (OVERRULING), conversational reading comprehension (COQA) (p. 6, Table 2 p. 7)
size: 12 commercial LLM APIs from 5 providers (Table 1, p. 7); HEADLINES 10,000, OVERRULING 2,400 and COQA 7,982 examples, each split at random into a training set for learning the cascade and a test set (p. 6, Table 2 p. 7); cascade length 3 (p. 6).
evaluation: task accuracy against gold answers, traded off against API cost in USD: cost needed to match the best single LLM (Table 3, p. 8) and accuracy-cost curves (Figure 5, p. 9). No reasoning or step evaluation.

engtrace_use.sentence: Inspired by recent advances in process supervision (Lightman et al., 2023) and cascaded model verification (Chen et al., 2023), we introduce a two-stage evaluation framework that validates intermediate reasoning steps in addition to final-answer accuracy through a tiered verification protocol. (Section 4, L390-395)
engtrace_use.explanation: FrugalGPT is a cost-reduction method for LLM API use (title; abstract p. 1). Its LLM cascade does contain a check before escalation: a generation scoring function rates how reliable an answer is, and the cascade returns the answer if the score exceeds a threshold and otherwise queries the next, costlier API (p. 5; on HEADLINES the learned cascade is GPT-J, J1-L, GPT-4 with thresholds 0.96 and 0.37, p. 6). So 'cascaded' is right, and the May Tier 1 to Tier 2 escalation 'to optimize computational efficiency' (L496-504) does follow this pattern. 'Model verification' mislabels it: the scorer is a DistilBERT regressor trained on labelled examples from the same distribution to route queries (pp. 5-6, p. 10), the tasks are classification and reading comprehension (p. 6), and nothing in the paper verifies reasoning, checks steps or evaluates models. Listing it beside process supervision as an advance in 'verification' overstates its bearing on step validation; the citation map flags the same mismatch (C14a).

suggested_wording: Like an LLM cascade (Chen et al., 2023), which queries a costlier model only when a cheaper stage's answer is scored unreliable, the evaluator sends to the judge only the milestones and steps that its deterministic checks cannot settle.
facts_to_cite: FrugalGPT outlines three ways to cut the cost of LLM APIs: prompt adaptation, LLM approximation and LLM cascade (p. 1, pp. 2-5).

An LLM cascade sends a query to a list of LLM APIs in order and returns the first answer whose reliability score, from a generation scoring function, exceeds a threshold; otherwise it queries the next API (p. 5).
The scoring function is a simple regression model trained to predict whether an answer is correct; the experiments use DistilBERT (p. 5, p. 6).
On HEADLINES the learned cascade calls GPT-J, then J1-L, then GPT-4, accepting an answer at scores above 0.96 and 0.37 (p. 6), at 80% lower cost and 1.5% higher accuracy than GPT-4 (p. 7, Figure 3).
Cost savings needed to match the best single LLM: 98.3% on HEADLINES, 73.3% on OVERRULING and 59.2% on COQA (Table 3, p. 8).
Evaluated with 12 commercial LLM APIs from 5 providers on financial-news classification, legal overruling classification and conversational reading comprehension (pp. 6-7).
Learning the cascade needs labelled examples from the same or a similar distribution as the test queries (p. 10).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares only a design pattern: a cheap first stage with escalation of the rest to a costlier model, which is the shape of EngTrace's evaluator (deterministic checks first, then the MiMo judge on the residue; judged fraction 0.112 to 0.252 per model; state brief section 2). It lacks every benchmark property: no generated instances, no gold traces, no step-level evaluation, no engineering or STEM content, no human or expert validation, and its escalation rule is a learned reliability score rather than a deterministic check.

Its one bearing on the planned paragraph is the cost-motivated cascade (p. 5). EngTrace's evaluator is now a cascade whose first tier is deterministic: E5's judge sees only the milestones E3's match missed, and the router sends to MiMo the steps the digit rule does not flag (state brief section 2).
